newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Earnings cast shadow on hi-techs.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Earnings cast shadow on hi-techs.

text.p: A rash of high-tech companies lowering their profit expectations for the quarter ended September 30 is stirring concerns in the equity options market, option traders said.

"They've had a nice run since late summer," said a trader at an investment bank. "But you still get a little earnings surprise every now and then on the downside for some of those companies, and they're getting really banged."
Hubert Lee, senior option strategist at R.F. Lafferty & Co, agreed that recent remarks on lower profit expectations by some firms were casting a shadow over the market.
"If we continue to get these every couple of days, that may not be so great and people may not be willing to go so much for high-tech out-of-the money options," he said.
Wall Data Inc, whose stock plummetted 9-1/4 to 14, and Peak Technologies Group Inc, which tumbled 9-7/8 to 11-7/8, were the latest examples of the volatile earnings-induced swings, Lee noted.

Wall Data said Wednesday it expected a loss of $0.06-0.11 a share for the third quarter. Its puts and calls on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) saw heavier than usual traffic in the 15 strike for October and Janauary.
Peak, which said Wednesday it expected its third-quarter profits to be below analysts' estimates, does not have listed options yet.

Among the most actively traded options today, BMC Software Inc, whose volume in underlying stock was also more than double the usual levels, saw its November 90 calls trade 3,555 contracts to top CBOE's most actives list.

Most of the volume was in a two-by-one ratio vertical spread with November 85 calls. Traders were unsure of the strategy behind the trade, but some said it could be related to expectations on the company's earnings.
Rod Jamieson, vice president of option strategy at EVEREN Securities, said weak earnings news should not really be a surprise, given the bleak earnings for the second quarter.
"I would have thought, after the last quarter, expectations would be low already," Jamieson said.
"In most of those stocks, people have negative expectations," he added. "But one problem is, those negative expectations don't reflect in the stock prices now because they all had huge rallies."
